parameter_semantics: manipulated_object_pose_field selects the freshly observed world pose of the block that defines the Cartesian action frame. destination_pose_field selects the observed desired placement pose used as object-relative conditioning. Pose positions are metres and quaternions are wxyz; both fields are resolved in both causal frames, and the object field is resolved again for each executed action.
output_semantics: Each slot is [object-frame TCP translation xyz in metres, object-frame TCP rotation represented by the first two rotation-matrix columns (6D), native gripper scalar]. At training slot k, the frame is object_pose in the pre-action observation for that same slot. At execution, slots 1..8 are decoded against the fresh current object_pose, not the chunk-start pose. Rotation 6D is Gram-Schmidt projected to SO(3); the resulting relative pose is left-multiplied by the live object world pose. panda_kinematics.solve_ik converts that world TCP target to seven absolute joint targets from freshly measured qpos; the gripper scalar is appended unchanged and the executor applies its declared binary sign rule.

conversion_check.description: Compare FK of the IK-produced joint target with the demonstrated commanded TCP target after object-relative encode/decode, plus unchanged gripper scalar. Maximum position metres, rotation radians, and gripper error must be at most 0.005; nonunique joints are allowed. The only pose projection is 6D Gram-Schmidt, exact for encoded labels.

cut_relation: Uses every assigned [680,1160) action from all twelve demonstrations. It preserves the 680:840 retrieval overlap and 900:1160 close-drawer overlap while changing only the learned Cartesian coordinates to a live object frame. The intended refinement is object-displacement equivariance during attached transport; the post-release tail remains supervised for handoff robustness.
